result.topic_en: Latin notes from Riemann's Paris prize essay on heat conduction, deriving an expression for the curvature quantity k as a quotient of quadratic forms in the differentials and relating it to $dd(ds^2)$ divided by $4\Delta^2$.
result.transcription:
Primis duabus harum aequationum $\varphi$ satisfieri facile ex aequationibus (1) [?] requiritur. Tertia dat
$k = -\frac{3}{2}\,\frac{\sum_{\iota\iota'\iota''\iota'''}\left(\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}}\right)_0 \varepsilon_{\iota''}\varepsilon_{\iota'''}\,\delta\varepsilon_\iota\,\delta\varepsilon_{\iota'}}{\sum_{\iota\iota'} a^0_{\iota\iota'}\,\delta\varepsilon_\iota\,\delta\varepsilon_{\iota'}}$
vel quod idem est.
$k = -\frac{3}{2}\,\frac{\sum\left(\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}}\right)_0 \varepsilon_{\iota''}\varepsilon_{\iota'''}\,\delta\varepsilon_\iota\,\delta\varepsilon_{\iota'}}{\sum a^0_{\iota\iota'}\varepsilon_\iota\varepsilon_{\iota'}\,\sum a^0_{\iota\iota'}\delta\varepsilon_\iota\delta\varepsilon_{\iota'} - \left(\sum a^0_{\iota\iota'}\varepsilon_\iota\delta\varepsilon_{\iota'}\right)^2}$
et quum hujus expressionis numerator et denominator sit functio homogenea secundi gradus quantitatum
$\varepsilon_\iota\,\delta\varepsilon_{\iota'} - \varepsilon_{\iota'}\,\delta\varepsilon_\iota$
[-loco $\varepsilon$ scribere possum-] $\varepsilon_\iota\ \delta\varepsilon_\iota$ substituere possumus $s_\iota$ [?] $\delta x_\iota$, vel etiam $dx_\iota\ \delta x_\iota$
$k = -\frac{3}{2}\,\frac{dd(\delta\delta)}{4\Delta^2}$

methods.what: Expression of the curvature k at a point as a ratio of the second derivatives of the metric coefficients (contracted with two direction vectors) to the norm of the metric form
Equivalent form of k with the Gram determinant (squared area of the parallelogram spanned by the two directions) in the denominator
Observation that numerator and denominator are homogeneous of second degree in the bivector components, allowing substitution of differentials
